A gearshift mechanism includes a shift lever that can pivot around two separate axes. It also includes a sensor arrangement having two sensor tracks, together with a sensor-actuating element carried by a movable carrier positioned within a housing. This carrier is connected to the shift lever so that movement of the lever causes the sensor-actuating element to travel relative to the sensors.

The carrier is supported for movement by a guide structure inside the housing and is joined through a hinge connection to a link, which is in turn connected to the shift lever. The gearshift assembly includes a shift lever configured to pivot about two distinct axes, referred to as the first axis and the second axis. This dual-axis movement allows the shift lever to be displaced in different directions corresponding to different gear selection or shifting operations.

Within the assembly, a sensor triggering element is mounted on a movable element carrier. The element carrier is positioned inside a housing and is arranged so that its movement can be detected by sensors located along defined sensing paths. The sensor triggering element cooperates with these sensors to indicate the position or movement of the shift lever.

The element carrier is mechanically coupled to the shift lever by a link. This link is connected by hinges, allowing relative movement between the shift lever and the element carrier while still transmitting motion from the shift lever to the carrier. As a result, movement of the shift lever is converted into controlled movement of the element carrier and the sensor triggering element.

When the shift lever pivots about the first axis, this motion causes the element carrier to move linearly along a first path of sensors. During this linear displacement, the sensor triggering element passes along or near the first path, enabling the sensors to detect the corresponding shift lever position.

When the shift lever pivots about the second axis, the element carrier causes the sensor triggering element to pivot along a second path of sensors. In this case, the triggering element follows a different sensing path, allowing the assembly to distinguish movement about the second axis from movement about the first axis.

In this way, the gearshift assembly converts two-axis pivoting movement of the shift lever into distinct movements of the sensor triggering element along separate sensor paths, enabling reliable detection of the shift lever’s position and operation.
outputs.L4:
A gearshift assembly includes a shift lever that can be moved by a vehicle operator to select different gearshift positions. The shift lever is mounted so that it is pivotable about two different axes. Pivoting about a first axis may correspond, for example, to movement of the lever in one shift direction, while pivoting about a second axis may correspond to movement in another shift direction, such as a selection direction. In this way, the lever can perform the typical movements required for selecting and engaging different gears.

The assembly further includes a sensor assembly arranged to detect the movements or positions of the shift lever. The sensor assembly has two sensor paths, each associated with a different type or direction of movement of the shift lever. A sensor-triggering element is provided for cooperating with the sensor paths. This sensor-triggering element may be, for example, a magnet, a conductive element, an optical marker, or another component capable of being detected by the sensors of the sensor assembly.

The sensor-triggering element is carried by a guided carrier that is mechanically linked to the shift lever. The connection between the shift lever and the carrier is arranged so that movements of the shift lever are converted into corresponding movements of the carrier. When the shift lever pivots about the first axis, the carrier is guided in a substantially linear direction. This linear displacement causes the sensor-triggering element to move along or relative to one of the sensor paths, thereby allowing the sensor assembly to detect the lever movement associated with the first axis.

When the shift lever pivots about the second axis, the carrier does not primarily move linearly. Instead, the carrier pivots or tilts in response to the lever movement. This pivoting movement causes the sensor-triggering element to interact with the other sensor path of the sensor assembly. As a result, the sensor assembly can distinguish movement of the shift lever about the second axis from movement about the first axis.

By using a carrier that is capable of both guided linear movement and pivoting movement, the gearshift assembly translates two-axis movement of the shift lever into clearly distinguishable sensor signals. The two sensor paths provide separate detection of the different gearshift movements, allowing the system to determine the position or movement direction of the shift lever accurately. This arrangement may be used in an electronic or shift-by-wire gearshift system, where mechanical lever movements are converted into electrical signals for controlling a transmission.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may be small, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called the definite article because it points to something specific. When we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book—we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

“The” helps make communication clear. It can refer to something already mentioned, something unique, or something known by context. For example, “the sun” refers to the one sun we see in the sky, and “the teacher” may refer to a specific teacher in a classroom.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” appears everywhere in English writing and speech. It gives sentences structure, precision, and meaning. Without it, many phrases would sound incomplete or unclear. In this way, **“the” is a tiny word with a very large role**.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a gearshift assembly with a pivoting shift lever, sensor paths, and a movable sensor triggering element carried by a guided element carrier.
counterfactuals.output: A gearshift assembly for a vehicle transmission includes a shift lever mounted for pivotal movement relative to a housing along at least one shift path. A sensor arrangement is provided for detecting selected positions of the shift lever, the sensor arrangement including a plurality of sensor paths associated with respective shift positions or shift gates. A guided element carrier is coupled to the shift lever and is movable in response to pivotal movement of the shift lever. A sensor triggering element is carried by the guided element carrier and is displaceable relative to the sensor paths such that, during movement of the shift lever, the sensor triggering element selectively cooperates with sensors disposed along the sensor paths to generate position signals indicative of the position or operating state of the gearshift assembly. The guided element carrier constrains movement of the sensor triggering element along a defined trajectory, thereby improving positional accuracy and reducing tolerance-related detection errors.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical description of an automotive gearshift position sensor mechanism where lever motion about one axis causes linear carrier travel and motion about another axis causes carrier pivoting.
counterfactuals.output:
An automotive gearshift position sensor mechanism can be implemented as a two-degree-of-freedom mechanical converter in which angular movement of the shift lever is transformed into two distinct motions of a sensor carrier: linear translation and pivotal rotation.

The mechanism includes a gearshift lever supported in a pivot housing so that the lever can move about two substantially orthogonal axes. Movement of the lever about a first axis, corresponding for example to a fore-aft shift direction, is mechanically coupled to a carrier member through a guide, pin, cam, link, or yoke arrangement. As the lever rotates about this first axis, the coupling converts the angular lever displacement into substantially linear travel of the carrier along a defined path. The carrier may slide in guide rails or slots formed in a sensor housing, ensuring repeatable displacement corresponding to selected gear positions.

Movement of the lever about a second axis, corresponding for example to a lateral gate-selection direction, acts on the same carrier in a different manner. Instead of translating the carrier, lever rotation about the second axis applies a moment to the carrier, causing the carrier to pivot about a carrier pivot axis. This pivoting may be produced by an offset drive pin, cam surface, fork engagement, or spherical joint arranged so that lateral lever displacement rotates the carrier relative to the housing while permitting or accommodating its linear sliding movement.

The carrier supports one or more sensor targets, such as magnets, conductive elements, optical flags, or coded tracks. Stationary sensing elements, such as Hall-effect sensors, inductive sensors, potentiometric contacts, optical detectors, or magnetic field sensors, are mounted to the housing adjacent the carrier travel path. Linear displacement of the carrier changes the sensed position along one coordinate, while pivotal displacement changes the sensed position along a second coordinate. The combined carrier translation and rotation therefore encode the two-dimensional position of the gearshift lever.

In operation, when the driver moves the lever in the shift direction, the lever rotates about the first axis and drives the carrier linearly. When the driver moves the lever in the select direction, the lever rotates about the second axis and pivots the carrier. When the lever is moved through a normal H-pattern or multi-gate shift path, the carrier undergoes a corresponding combination of translation and pivoting. The sensor assembly interprets these two motions to determine the selected gear or shift-gate position.

This arrangement allows the position sensor to be compact because both lever axes are monitored using a single movable carrier. It also provides mechanical separation of the two input motions: one lever axis produces predominantly linear carrier travel, while the other lever axis produces predominantly angular carrier displacement. As a result, the sensor can generate reliable position signals with reduced packaging volume, simplified assembly, and improved alignment between the mechanical shift pattern and the electrical position output.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for a vehicle shifter assembly including first and second sensor paths, a triggering element on a movable carrier, a guide structure, hinge connection, and link coupled to the shift lever.
counterfactuals.output: A vehicle shifter assembly includes a shift lever movable between a plurality of shift positions and a sensing arrangement configured to detect movement of the shift lever. The sensing arrangement includes a carrier movable relative to first and second sensor paths and supporting a triggering element configured to selectively interact with the first and second sensor paths. A link couples the carrier to the shift lever such that movement of the shift lever drives movement of the carrier and the triggering element relative to the first and second sensor paths. The first and second sensor paths provide position signals corresponding to respective positions or movement ranges of the shift lever, enabling detection of a selected gear position or shift state.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a gearshift assembly in which a sensor triggering element follows different sensor paths depending on whether the shift lever pivots about a first or second axis.
counterfactuals.output:
A gearshift assembly comprising a shift lever mounted for selective pivotal movement about a first pivot axis and about a second pivot axis distinct from the first pivot axis, the shift lever being operatively coupled to a sensor triggering element. The sensor triggering element is arranged to actuate or influence at least one position sensor during movement of the shift lever.

The sensor triggering element is guided or displaced along a first sensor path when the shift lever is pivoted about the first pivot axis, and is guided or displaced along a second sensor path, different from the first sensor path, when the shift lever is pivoted about the second pivot axis. The first and second sensor paths are spatially offset and/or differently oriented relative to the at least one position sensor, such that movement of the shift lever about the first pivot axis produces a first sensor signal pattern and movement of the shift lever about the second pivot axis produces a second sensor signal pattern distinguishable from the first sensor signal pattern.

In one embodiment, the sensor triggering element comprises a magnetic, ferromagnetic, optical, inductive, capacitive, or mechanical actuating member carried by or coupled to the shift lever. The at least one position sensor is disposed adjacent to the first and second sensor paths and is configured to detect the presence, position, displacement, or trajectory of the sensor triggering element. By causing the sensor triggering element to follow different sensor paths depending on the pivot axis about which the shift lever is moved, the gearshift assembly enables determination of a selected shift direction, shift gate, or gear-selection operation based on the detected path of the sensor triggering element.

In particular, the gearshift assembly may comprise a support structure defining the first pivot axis and the second pivot axis, wherein the first pivot axis corresponds to a selecting movement of the shift lever and the second pivot axis corresponds to a shifting movement of the shift lever. The sensor triggering element is kinematically linked to the shift lever such that pivotal movement about the first pivot axis displaces the sensor triggering element along the first sensor path, while pivotal movement about the second pivot axis displaces the sensor triggering element along the second sensor path. The first and second sensor paths are configured so that the sensor signals generated thereby are unambiguously assignable to the respective pivotal movements of the shift lever.
